Title: UmbraDesktop
Description: An OS-style windowed desktop for the Umbraco backoffice. Open your sections as real windows and work in several of them side by side, instead of one thing at a time.

AuthorDetails.Name: Luuk Peters
AuthorDetails.Description: Umbraco developer building packages that extend the CMS with enterprise-grade features.

Screenshots.Caption: Content and media open as separate windows, side by side, with the taskbar below.

Your work, guarded three ways at once: a dot for unsaved changes, a warning when someone else saved over you, and an error when they binned it. Every marker is repeated on the taskbar, so it reaches a window you minimised an hour ago.
The launcher: your pinned apps at the top, everything else grouped by what it does, including the commercial packages you have installed and a Games group from the optional add-on.
The macOS theme: traffic lights on every title bar, a floating dock, and the backoffice in dark mode.
The Windows 98 theme: grey chrome, navy title bars, and the launcher as a Start menu.
Desktop settings: pick your chrome theme and your background, from the eight that ship or any image already in your Media Library. Both are remembered per user.
Background Jobs: every scheduled job Umbraco runs behind your site, with how often each runs, when it last ran and when it is due next. Umbraco shows this nowhere else.

With Umbraco AI installed, its Copilot chat opens as a window and the agent can put a page on your desk beside it. Here it read the desk, found the homepage and opened it, and the conversation is still there to carry on with.
The way in: the desktop icon in the backoffice header, between Help and your avatar.

RelatedPackages.Description: Games for the desktop, starting with Minesweeper. Released from the same tag and always the same version. Entirely optional: the desktop is unchanged without it.
